checks: unknown xattr does not disable status
unknown xattr does not disable status

gate.default: Status disabled; enable with SL7_MOUNT_STATUS=1 or benchmark --settle-mode quiescent.
gate.contract: Root-only read-only user.sl7.status JSON. Drained includes queued inode overflow, active seal jobs, reads and native I/O. Quiescent additionally requires closed FUSE handles, no fatal worker failure and no shutdown. Waits require three quiet observations with matching progress counters, and reject sealing errors.
gate.tests: The status remains busy while a sealing worker is deliberately paused. Overflow queue bits count even when the hot queue is empty. Mounted tests cover open/closed handles, completed sealing, reconstruction, unknown xattrs, size negotiation and ERANGE in both pipeline modes.
limitations: An observation for isolated workloads; not an fsync barrier or a guarantee against future client activity.
Diagnostic support preserves ENOSYS behavior when disabled. Enabling it may change kernel xattr request behavior, so quiescent runs are a separately identified benchmark method.
Historical CPU-idle mode remains the default for existing comparisons.
Two reversed-order rounds on a shared node, not a statistical significance claim.
Warm OS caches; debug incremental only.
Quiescence is observed through the root status attribute after builds and executable checks; diagnostic support may change kernel xattr request behavior.
Cumulative phase times overlap; they are not added Cargo latency.

Two workers in both SL7 cases; fixed source/profile/output paths; both use the same binary and opt-in status diagnostic, with the pipeline disabled or enabled; every SL7 stage waits for closed handles and drained work.
